newsitem.title: Italy: Ramshackle flotilla ferries Albanians to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Ramshackle flotilla ferries Albanians to Italy.

text.p: Hundreds of Albanians fled to Italy to escape armed anarchy on Friday in a ramshackle flotilla of rusting gunboats, fishing vessels and launches.

At least 16 Albanian navy vessels, most of them small patrol boats built decades ago by the Chinese, limped into southern Italian ports under escort after crawling across the Adriatic with deserting servicemen and civilians.
"The Albanians are arriving here in boats that are completely unseaworthy," a senior Italian naval officer said.
"God only knows how they made it," added a police officer.

Though the numbers were relatively low, the unfolding exodus raised fears in Italy of a repeat of the tide of 40,000 Albanians who flocked to southeast ports on an armada of ships in 1991 after Stalinist rule crumbled in Europe's poorest state.

Twelve of the boats, their paint flaked and hulls rusted, made it into the port of Brindisi, where Italian armed forces were also preparing to receive hundreds of foreigners evacuated from Albania in a multinational military air and sea rescue.
The larger vessels had their gun turrets covered with tarpaulins and an Italian naval officer said security forces had collected about 400 rifles and automatic weapons.

One of the patrol boats, which had set out from the Albanian port of Vlore before dawn, reached Brindisi with 177 people crammed on the deck, almost all of them civilians including about 10 children and at least two pregnant women.

"We don't understand anything that's happening at home any more. Everyone has weapons in the south and in the north," said one man who disembarked after police used sniffer dogs to search the human cargo for drugs.

Albania's former defence minister Safet Zhulali, removed this week when embattled President Sali Berisha agreed to set up a national unity government in the face of armed rebellion, was among those fleeing the unrest in the small Balkan state.
Berisha's son and daughter, accompanied by armed bodyguards, fled to Italy on Thursday on a ferry from the port of Durres.
Italian coastguards said Zhulalu, his wife and their 14-year-old daughter were among about 70 Albanians who arrived in Brindisi on Friday on the merchant ship Fulgidus.
Navy and coastguard officers said at least another nine vessels, from fishing boats to freighters, had either docked or were heading for southern ports with more than 200 refugees.
An Albanian military helicopter, the latest of several to fly to Italy, also landed on Friday near the port of Bari where its three crew put themselves in the hands of police.

Italy, a magnet for Albanian illegal immigrants, has sought to discourage refugees since protests sparked by the collapse of shady saving schemes erupted this month into armed insurrection in southern Albania.
The U.N. refugee agency said on Friday that it had urged Italy and Greece to allow fleeing Albanians to enter and stay "as long as necessary".

"At the moment only a limited number of individuals have left Albania. Some fled targeted violence and apparently others fled the general conflict situation," spokesman Kris Janowski of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said.
"Nevertheless, we are in close contact with the governments of Italy and Greece and are discussing arrangements for a possible influx of people," Janowski said in Geneva.
Greece, which shares a border with Albania, and Italy said they had made preparations to cope with any influx.

"We are dealing...with a state that is falling apart. Italy faces the very serious risk that its coasts will be invaded by people fleeing a dramatic situation," Italy's deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said.
